subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Trans fatty acids in the diet are of particular concern because they:
options: Have no effect on blood cholesterol
Lower LDL and raise HDL cholesterol
Raise LDL and lower HDL cholesterol
questions.explain: Trans fats raise harmful LDL while lowering protective HDL cholesterol, increasing CHD risk.

questions.q: A person with coeliac disease must avoid:
options: Gluten found in wheat, barley and rye
questions.explain: Coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten, so wheat, barley and rye must be avoided.

questions.q: Which micro-organism is deliberately and usefully employed in bread-making?
questions.explain: Yeast is a useful micro-organism that ferments sugars to leaven bread and brew alcohol.

questions.q: The browning of a cut apple left exposed to air is caused by:
questions.explain: Enzymes (polyphenol oxidases) react with oxygen on cut surfaces, producing brown pigments.

questions.q: 'Food provenance' refers to:
options: Where and how food was grown, reared or caught
The number of calories in a food
The retail price of the food
questions.explain: Provenance concerns the origin and production method of food, increasingly important to consumers.

questions.q: Type-2 diabetes is characterised by:
options: Complete absence of insulin from birth
The body's cells becoming resistant to insulin
questions.explain: In type-2 diabetes cells become resistant to insulin, so blood glucose is poorly controlled.

questions.q: Which pathogen is particularly associated with undercooked poultry and is a leading cause of food poisoning in the UK?
questions.explain: Campylobacter, often from raw or undercooked poultry, is the most common bacterial cause of UK food poisoning.

questions.q: To check that cooked food has reached a safe internal temperature, it should reach a core temperature of at least:
questions.explain: A core temperature of 75 degrees C ensures harmful bacteria in the centre of the food are destroyed.

questions.q: Salting and sugaring preserve foods primarily by:
options: Reducing the water activity available to micro-organisms
questions.explain: High salt or sugar concentrations draw water out by osmosis, lowering aw and inhibiting microbes.

questions.q: Listeria monocytogenes is of special concern because, unlike most pathogens, it can:
questions.explain: Listeria can multiply slowly at fridge temperatures, posing a risk in chilled ready-to-eat foods.

questions.q: Which is the basic structural unit of a triglyceride?
options: One glucose and three fatty acids
One glycerol and three fatty acids
Three glycerols and one fatty acid
Three amino acids and one glycerol
questions.explain: A triglyceride consists of one glycerol molecule esterified with three fatty acids.

questions.q: Caramelisation differs from the Maillard reaction because it involves:
options: A reaction of proteins with sugars
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar alone when heated, without amino acids.

questions.q: Irradiation as a preservation method works by:
options: Using ionising radiation to destroy micro-organisms and pests
questions.explain: Irradiation exposes food to ionising radiation, killing micro-organisms and extending shelf life.

questions.q: Which is an example of an ethical factor influencing food choice?
options: Selecting a familiar brand by habit
Choosing free-range eggs on animal-welfare grounds
Choosing food because it is cheapest
questions.explain: Ethical choices, such as welfare-friendly or fair-trade products, are based on moral concerns.

questions.q: Lecithin in egg yolk acts as an emulsifier in mayonnaise because it:
options: Raises the pH of the mixture
Thickens the mixture by absorbing water
Coagulates the oil into solid particles
Has one part attracted to oil and one part attracted to water
questions.explain: An emulsifier has hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends, holding oil and water together as a stable emulsion.

questions.q: The temperature 'danger zone' in which bacteria multiply most readily is approximately:
questions.explain: Between about 5 and 63 degrees C bacteria multiply rapidly, so foods should not be held there.

questions.q: Omega-3 fatty acids found in oily fish are classified as:
questions.explain: Omega-3s contain several double bonds, making them polyunsaturated and beneficial for the heart.

questions.q: 'Food security' is best defined as:
options: Selling food at a high price
All people having reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
questions.explain: Food security means everyone has consistent access to enough safe, nutritious food for a healthy life.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is most directly linked to a long-term deficiency of:
questions.explain: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D reduce bone mineral density, leading to brittle bones.

questions.q: Which provides the most kilojoules of energy per gram?
questions.explain: Fat provides about 37 kJ per gram, more than double that of carbohydrate or protein.

questions.q: Combining beans on toast to obtain a full set of essential amino acids is an example of:
questions.explain: Protein complementation combines two LBV foods whose limiting amino acids differ to give the full set.

questions.q: Adding lemon juice to cut fruit slows enzymic browning because:
options: The acidity inhibits the enzyme activity
questions.explain: The low pH of lemon juice denatures the browning enzymes, slowing the reaction.

questions.q: A food described as containing high biological value (HBV) protein is one that:
options: Contains all the essential amino acids
Contains no amino acids at all
questions.explain: HBV proteins supply all the indispensable (essential) amino acids the body cannot synthesise.

questions.q: Lactose, the sugar found in milk, is composed of which two monosaccharides?
questions.explain: Lactose is a disaccharide of glucose and galactose joined by a glycosidic bond.

questions.q: During the shortening of pastry, fat performs which function?
options: Coats the flour and prevents long gluten strands forming
Acts as a raising agent producing gas
questions.explain: Fat coats flour particles, limiting gluten development and giving a short, crumbly texture.

questions.q: Vacuum packing helps preserve food chiefly by:
options: Heating the food to sterilise it
Removing oxygen so aerobic spoilage organisms cannot grow
Adding sugar to lower water activity
questions.explain: Removing oxygen inhibits aerobic micro-organisms and slows oxidative spoilage of the food.

questions.q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble?
options: Vitamins A, D, E and K
questions.explain: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fat and can be stored in the body's fatty tissues.

questions.q: A 'use by' date on a food label indicates:
options: The date the food was made
A guide to best quality only
The date after which the food may be unsafe to eat
questions.explain: 'Use by' relates to food safety; the food should not be eaten after this date.

questions.q: Which carbohydrate is a monosaccharide?
questions.explain: Glucose is a single-sugar unit, whereas sucrose, lactose and maltose are disaccharides.

questions.q: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is defined as the energy needed to:
options: Maintain essential body functions at complete rest
questions.explain: BMR is the energy required to sustain basic functions such as respiration and circulation at rest.
